Source is Section 1.01 (Defined Terms), a definitions article containing many independent defined terms declared back-to-back; each was extracted as its own WireDefinition per the multiple-definitions rule, including terms with no covenant-quantitative content (e.g. Board of Directors, Capital Stock) rather than only the apparently 'salient' ones.

Two terms ('Beneficial Ownership Certification', 'Borrowers') are pure or near-pure cross-references outside the supplied source; getReferencedProvision was attempted for the 'Borrowers' preliminary-statements reference and did not resolve (confirmed via tool call). The Section 4.01(h) and Section 2.03 cross-references had already been flagged out-of-scope (source-context budget exhausted) by the prior retrieval pass, so those were not re-attempted per the no-duplicate-request policy.

'Borrowing Minimum' and 'Borrowing Multiple' are structurally piecewise-by-currency; the four fixed-dollar cases were represented with a best-effort IF/COMPARE currency-selector (flagged as an IR extension candidate gap) and the genuinely variable 'other Alternative Currency' case was correctly left UNSUPPORTED rather than guessed. All 6 frozen-inventory VALUE/MATERIAL items were consumed on their corresponding MONEY nodes and at each definition's top level.

The two detected 0.00% floor values and the December 31, 2018 GAAP-freeze date (not covered by named inventory items) were represented respectively in 'Canadian Prime Rate' (MAX floor) and 'Capitalized Lease Obligation' (AS_OF date anchor).

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: A construct that selects among a fixed set of labeled values based on matching a discrete, non-numeric transaction attribute (here, the Borrowing's currency) against named cases, analogous to SCHEDULE's date-ranged case selection but for discrete/categorical keys.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: SCHEDULE's cases are keyed by date ranges (from/to), not discrete labels. COMPARE/IF require both sides to be the same value type drawn from MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO/PERCENT-like literals, and there is no CURRENCY or generic ENUM literal kind, so comparing a TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE's currency against a fixed currency label has no clean, type-safe representation - forcing an ad hoc equality of two reference-kind nodes that the schema's type discipline does not clearly sanction.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: A CASE_SELECT node (operand: the discrete key expression, e.g. a TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE; cases: [{matchValue (a literal or DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE label), value}]; defaultValue) mirroring SCHEDULE's shape but for discrete/categorical keys such as currency, jurisdiction, or facility Type.
